A.name: Informational prompt only
A.description: Keep current auto-resume behavior on continuation keywords. Remove wording that asks user to reply 'yes'. Treat prompt as a status notification.
files_to_modify: gateway/run.py - _resolve_resume_checkpoint_decision: simplify prompt text, keep keyword heuristic
A.backward_compatibility: HIGH - existing behavior preserved; only prompt wording changes.
risks: Users may still misinterpret the prompt if wording not fully neutral.
Does not satisfy the explicit-confirmation requirement stated by the user.

B.name: Strict confirmation flow
B.description: When a checkpoint exists and the incoming message is not an explicit confirmation, display the prompt, record a pending-confirmation state, and do NOT start the agent. The next incoming message resolves the pending state: 'yes' triggers resume, anything else starts fresh and clears the checkpoint.
files_to_modify: gateway/run.py - _resolve_resume_checkpoint_decision: split into (a) detect-and-prompt returning 'awaiting_confirmation', (b) resolve-pending-state on next message
gateway/run.py - message handler: gate agent.run_conversation when a pending confirmation exists; consume confirmation reply first
agent/turn_context.py - build_turn_context: handle resume_checkpoint_decision='awaiting_confirmation' or ensure no resume occurs until explicit
agent/execution_checkpoint.py: optional helper to mark/validate confirmation
hermes_state.py: optional pending_resume_checkpoints table or in-memory only (in-memory sufficient per gateway instance)
B.backward_compatibility: MODERATE - users typing 'continue' without 'yes' will no longer auto-resume; this matches the prompt but breaks prior muscle memory.
risks: Gateway restart while pending loses state (unless persisted; persistence adds complexity).
Session lock / busy handling must not block confirmation message.
A stray unrelated message could clear checkpoint if user sends it by accident while pending.
Needs careful handling of /stop, /queue, and control commands while pending.

analysis.current_behavior: The resume prompt asks for explicit 'yes' but auto-resumes on 'continue'/'resume' keywords. This is internally inconsistent.
analysis.user_requirement: Demonstrated expectation: continue -> prompt -> explicit yes -> resume. No keyword-fallback dependency.
analysis.state_required: A per-session pending-confirmation state must be introduced. No such state exists today.
analysis.persistence: In-memory state is enough for MVP; persisting pending state across gateway restart is optional and increases complexity.

rationale: The current prompt text already promises explicit confirmation, so the implementation should honor it.
Option B is the only path that satisfies the user's stated validation requirement (no keyword-fallback dependency).
Complexity is manageable because it is localized to the gateway message handler and resume-decision method.
The main risk (gateway restart losing pending state) can be mitigated by a short-lived pending state and a clear prompt re-send on restart.
